settings.gmail.setupHelp: Press Sign in with Google and approve read-only access in your browser: there is nothing to set up. If this copy of Lumen has no built-in Google sign-in, or you prefer your own Google Cloud project, open Advanced: in Google Cloud Console, enable the Gmail API, create an OAuth client of type Desktop app, and paste its Client ID and secret there (your own client is then used instead of Lumen’s). Either way Lumen asks only for read-only access to your mail (gmail.readonly), opens Google’s sign-in page in your normal browser, and keeps the tokens encrypted on this computer. The new-tab page only ever receives sender, subject and preview text.
settings.gmail.limits: Because you use your own Google Cloud project, Google’s limits for unverified apps apply: while the project is in Testing, only test users you add can connect, Google shows a “hasn’t verified this app” warning, and the connection ends every 7 days, so you connect again then. Publishing the project removes the 7-day limit.
settings.widgets.github.tokenSaved: Saved. Paste a new token to replace it.
settings.widgets.github.hideDrafts: Hide draft pull requests in review requests
settings.widgets.github.privacy: Titles of issues and pull requests from private repositories are fetched too, and Lumen keeps them in memory (they are not written to settings.json) and passes them to your new-tab pages to show them, so they can appear in a new tab’s history on this device. To keep a repository off the card, don’t give the token access to it.
settings.widgets.github.tokenHelp: Create a fine-grained personal access token at github.com/settings/personal-access-tokens: pick the repositories to include (or All repositories) and grant read-only Issues and Pull requests (Metadata: read is added automatically). No write permissions are needed. Unread notifications work only with a classic token that has the notifications scope, because GitHub doesn’t offer notifications to fine-grained tokens; without one, the card shows the two lists and says so. Stored encrypted by your system; it never reaches the new-tab page and is sent only to api.github.com.
settings.widgets.github.showHelp: Lists are refreshed every few minutes. If GitHub’s rate limit is reached, Lumen waits until it resets.
settings.widgets.feed.pickHint: Lumen fetches the feed itself; the new-tab page never goes online. Headlines open in a new tab.

widgets.muse.keySaved: Saved. Paste a new key to replace it.
widgets.muse.keyHelp: Create a key at dev.meta.ai (Meta Model API, public preview). It is stored encrypted by your system and never reaches the new-tab page or your settings file.
widgets.muse.privacy: What is sent, and the cost
widgets.muse.privacyHelp: Your prompt and every question you type go to Meta, and so do the answers it returns. Each answer uses your key’s credit (about $1.25 per million tokens in and $4.25 per million out, at the time of writing). The card asks about every six hours at most, or when you press Refresh or Ask; check Meta’s current terms and limits.
widgets.muse.promptHelp: Answered on the card. Keep it short: answers are capped at a few hundred words.
widgets.muse.modelHelp: Default muse-spark-1.3. Other names from dev.meta.ai work too (muse-spark-1.2, muse-spark-1.1).
widgets.muse.search: Ground answers with web search (shows sources)
widgets.muse.searchHelp: Web search uses a different Meta endpoint and can cost more.
widgets.muse.colorsHelp: Only the card’s surface and title follow it.
google.refused.title: Google didn’t accept this sign-in
google.refused.tips: Try signing in again in a tab instead of this pop-up (Ctrl-click the site’s sign-in button). If a VPN or proxy is on, turn it off. If Google still refuses, use the site’s other way to sign in, such as an email link or a passkey.
google.refused.debugger: An extension or automation tool is attached to this page, so Lumen couldn’t sign in to Google as a normal browser. Close that tool (or sign in in another tab) and try again.
google.refused.automation: Automation is on (Settings → Advanced → Automation), which opens Chromium’s remote-debugging pipe, and Google can treat a browser like that as automated. Turn automation off (Lumen restarts), then sign in again. You can turn it back on afterwards. If Google still refuses, try a tab instead of a pop-up, or use the site’s other way to sign in.
gmail.signin.done: You can close this tab and go back to Lumen, which finishes connecting Gmail.
gmail.signin.denied: Gmail was not connected. You can close this tab.
google.refused.tipsTab: Try again in a moment. If a VPN or proxy is on, turn it off and retry. If Google still refuses, use the site’s other way to sign in, such as an email link or a passkey.
